page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr9i.3xlarge is a high clock speed virtual server instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The system provides 12 dedicated vCPUs utilizing an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.4 GHz. System memory capacity totals 96.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB allocation per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of external network block storage for persistent filesystem requirements. Dedicated graphics accelerators are absent, with a GPU count of zero. Network connectivity is provisioned at a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the hardware profile.

The hardware configuration pairs an elevated CPU clock speed of 3.4 GHz with an expansive 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio, optimizing density for environments where execution frequency and RAM capacity dictate throughput. Eliminating onboard NVMe storage lowers hardware tier overhead but shifts IOPS dependency toward network storage. This profile matches in-memory databases, large cache tiers, electronic design automation, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr9i.3xlarge is a high clock speed, memory-dense server instance based on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, alongside 96.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation. The instance includes no onboard local storage, directing persistent input/output operations through network-attached storage options, and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Networking is configured with a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth. By uniting elevated base clock frequencies with large per-core memory capacity, the server maximizes resource density for operations that rely heavily on memory indexing and single-thread execution rates. It is structurally aligned with in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, enterprise analytics, and high-throughput transaction processing.
